chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhl, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Layth al-Muradi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mosque of al-Fadikh, why it was called the Mosque of al-Fadikh, so he said: 'The date palms are called al-Fadikh, therefore it is called the Mosque of al-Fadikh.'

key_terms.الْفَضِيخ: A term for date palms or a grove of them

ai.seo_question: Why is the mosque known as Masjid al-Fadikh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the mosque's name derives from the date palms (al-Fadikh) in the area, highlighting the common practice of naming sacred sites after local natural features. This etymological explanation underscores the historical continuity of worship locations in Medina, linking the physical landscape to spiritual significance in Shia scholarly tradition.
